 3                                            INTRODUCTION
 4          1.      Plaintiff and the proposed members of the Class (defined below) (“Class
 5 Members”) bring this class action lawsuit on behalf of all persons who entrusted

 6 Defendant with highly sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (“PII”) 1 and

 7 Protected Health Information (“PHI”) 2 (collectively “Private Information”) that was

 8 subsequently exposed in a data breach, which Defendant discovered on March 2, 2025
 9 (“Data Breach”).

10          2.      Plaintiff’s claims arise from Defendant’s failure to properly secure and
11 safeguard Private Information that was entrusted to it, and its accompanying

12 responsibility to store and transfer that information.

13          3.      Defendant is a management consulting firm based in Emeryville, California.
14 Defendant’s services span the fields of corporate finance, economics, disputes and

15 investigations, and performance improvement. Defendant also specializes in Chapter 11

16 reorganizations and turnaround consulting and has been hired to provide services in a

17 number of bankruptcy proceedings, including those involving the Catholic dioceses and

18 the Boy Scouts of America, among others.
19          4.      Defendant had numerous statutory, regulatory, contractual, and common
20 law duties and obligations, including those based on their affirmative representations to

21 Plaintiff and the Class, to keep their Private Information confidential, safe, secure, and

22 protected from unauthorized disclosure or access.

23

24   1

25   or trace an individual’s identity, either alone or when combined with other personal or identifying
     information. 2 C.F.R. § 200.79. At a minimum, it includes all information that on its face expressly
26   identifies an individual.
     2
       Protected health information is a category of information that refers to an individual’s medical records
27   and history, which is protected under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act. Inter alia,
     PHI includes test results, procedure descriptions, diagnoses, personal or family medical histories and data
28
     points applied to a set of demographic information for a particular patient.
